title: Introduction to Ethical Hacking

objectives.text: Explain the five elements of information security and name the attack that breaks each one
Classify an attack as passive, active, close-in, insider or distribution from a short scenario
Identify the hacker class and motive behind an attack, including APTs and insiders
State what makes a test ethical (authorization, scope, rules of engagement, NDA, report) and pick the right assessment type
Describe how AI tools help an ethical hacker and the limits on using them with client data
Put the five hacking phases, the CEH framework and the 7 Cyber Kill Chain stages in order, and map activity to them
Use MITRE ATT&CK, the Diamond Model and threat intelligence vocabulary (TTPs, IoCs, intelligence types)
Classify controls by type and function, choose a risk response and order the incident response phases
Match a scenario to the law or standard that applies (PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOX, GDPR, DPA, FISMA, GLBA, DMCA, ISO 27001)

readingMap.why: Know the five elements and the attack classes; the examples repeat what the notes cover.
Learn the class names and the one trait that defines each; skip the history.
Scope, authorization, test types and the new AI material are frequent scenario questions.
Phase and kill chain order, ATT&CK tactic vs technique and threat intelligence types are tested all through the exam.
Control functions, risk responses and the incident response order appear in many questions.
Regulation-matching questions: learn the quick-match table, not the legal history.

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a non-technical friend why an ethical hacker needs written permission, and what else must be agreed before the first test.
Walk through the five hacking phases with one concrete example each, then say which Cyber Kill Chain stage each example matches.
Explain the difference between a tactic, a technique and an indicator of compromise, and why defenders prefer detecting TTPs.
